categories.main_business_segments: Amentum operates as a single business segment, providing advanced engineering and technology solutions primarily to U.S. and allied government agencies, as well as select commercial enterprises. Its offerings span energy and environmental, intelligence, space, defense, civilian, and commercial end-markets, with a focus on full mission lifecycle solutions.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Amentum leverages advanced engineering, digital modernization, cybersecurity, intelligence analytics, C5ISR, environmental remediation, and RDT&E capabilities. The company employs model-based systems engineering, rapid prototyping, integrated sustainment, and advanced simulation, and is involved in the development of clean energy technologies, space systems, and digital transformation solutions.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The primary customers are U.S. federal government agencies, including the Department of Energy, Department of Defense, Intelligence Community, NASA, and Department of Homeland Security, accounting for about 90% of revenue. Internationally, Amentum serves allied governments such as the U.K. Ministry of Defence, U.K. Nuclear Decommissioning Authority, and the Australian Department of Defence, as well as select commercial clients in aerospace, space, automotive, and telecommunications.
categories.geographic_coverage: Amentum has a global footprint with operations in approximately 80 countries. Key regions include the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, Europe, and the Indo-Pacific, with significant business in both domestic and international defense and energy markets.
categories.supply_chain_position: Amentum primarily operates as a downstream solutions provider, serving as a prime contractor or subcontractor delivering engineering, technology, and lifecycle services directly to government and commercial end customers. The company also partners with other primes and participates in joint ventures for large, complex contracts.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Amentum's strategy emphasizes winning and executing large, complex government programs, expanding in high-growth areas such as cybersecurity, hypersonics, autonomy, space-based ISR, environmental remediation, and energy transition. The company invests in R&D for digital modernization, artificial intelligence, and advanced mission systems, and seeks to leverage cross-domain innovation and revenue synergies from its combined capabilities.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated primarily through long-term service contracts with government and commercial clients, using cost-plus-fee (62% of FY24 revenue), fixed-price (27%), and time-and-materials (11%) contract structures. The company benefits from a substantial backlog ($45.0 billion as of September 2024) and recurring revenue streams from multi-year contracts.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Amentum competes with major government services and defense contractors such as Booz Allen Hamilton, CACI, KBR, Leidos, ManTech, Parsons, Peraton, SAIC, V2X, Boeing, BAE Systems, General Dynamics, L3Harris, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, RTX, and others. It is positioned as a top-tier, large-scale, full-lifecycle solutions provider with broad technical capabilities and global reach.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the year ended September 27, 2024, Amentum reported $8.4 billion in revenue, with pro forma combined revenue (including the CMS acquisition) of $13.9 billion. The company has over 53,000 employees, a $45.0 billion backlog, and is focused on growth through new contract wins, expansion in high-growth markets, and leveraging its scale and diversity for operational efficiency.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Amentum differentiates itself through its scale, breadth of technical expertise, ability to deliver full mission lifecycle solutions, and deep, trusted relationships with government customers. Its unique value lies in its ability to address complex, high-priority challenges—such as digital modernization, energy transition, and national security—by integrating advanced technologies, a highly skilled workforce, and proven performance across diverse domains.
